      "partial_result": "## Verdict: REJECT\n\n**The smallest precise reason: if the anchor works perfectly, the gate still fails.** The anchor pulls the model toward the source, so the best it can do is make the candidate equal the source.\n- The source cc58377f measured 97.780925% R1 / 85.449629% mAP@R (`docs/inshop_late_dense_adaptation_gate_2026-09-30.md:7`).\n- The late100 control mean is 97.788794% / 85.514333%.\n- A candidate equal to the source scores \u22120.008pp R1 and \u22120.065pp mAP@R against the control, so it fails both fixed +0.20pp floors.\n- To pass, the anchored boundary-10 candidate must beat its own teacher by at least +0.208pp R1 and +0.265pp mAP@R.\n\nNothing in the contract supplies that gain:\n- The targets are a deterministic function of the source, computed on fit images whose labels CE already uses. The anchor adds no new information.\n- The only anchor gain in the ledger (+0.047 R1 / +0.81 mAP@R, one seed, no interval) came from a teacher about 2.1/5.1pp *stronger* than its student (`inshop_large_teacher_anchor_gate_2026-09-29.md`). Here the teacher is roughly as good as the control.\n- No freeze-boundary change in the ledger has moved R1 by more than 0.18pp (`inshop_dense_boundary_review_2026-09-29.md:22`). Unanchored, the added capacity measured \u22120.20/\u22120.29pp.\n- Prior art that gains from anchoring (L2-SP, DELTA, LwF, WiSE-FT, LP-FT) does so by keeping *pretrained* information the labels lack. Anchoring to a source fine-tuned on the same task has no such channel.\n- Your own ledger check already says the source/allocation distinction \"does not alone justify another loss-tweak experiment.\"\n\nThis bound is arithmetic from committed measurements, not a quality forecast.\n\n## Separate engineering risks (these matter even if the proposal is admitted)\n1. **The anchor needs a new step function.** `pe_large_optimization.step` hardcodes `loss=(ce+8*rank)*factor` (`scripts/pe_large_optimization.py:176`). Late100 only patched `coverage.terms` (`train_late_dense_adaptation.py:331`), and that route can only add the anchor by folding it into the logged CE. A new step means the \"unaltered driver\" claim must be proven again.\n2. **The shared prefix is required to pass the speed ratio.** Counting block forward costs (backward \u2248 2\u00d7 forward) predicts late100's candidate/control ratio of 52/48 = 1.083; measured median-step ratios were 1.082/1.084. Adding a teacher suffix of 14 blocks gives about 66/48 = 1.375. A separate whole teacher gives about 76/48 = 1.58, which fails the \u22641.50 cap.\n3. **The mechanics wall cap is nearly used up.** Late mechanics took 107.82s of the 120s cap (`late-dense-v1/mechanics-v1-receipt.json`). Its 26 executed updates at about +0.33s each for the teacher add roughly 8.6s, reaching about 116.4s. That leaves about 3.6s for two teacher reconstructions, the authentication hashes and the whole-source calibration. With \"no cap rescue,\" this probably ends the procedure on engineering grounds.\n4. **Host memory is nearly at the cap.** Mechanics peaked at 8,133,180 KiB against an 8,388,608 KiB cap, leaving 249 MiB. The F32 teacher suffix is about 705 MB. Any teacher copy or whole-source model built on the host breaks the cap.\n5. **CPU cannot prove the exact-zero initial anchor for the native run.** The CPU path runs F32 without autocast (`qualify_late_dense_adaptation_cpu.py:110`). Whether the FP16 gradient-enabled training student and the no-grad eval teacher produce identical bits can only be shown on GPU.\n\n## Actionable conditions if the parent overrides to ADMIT\n- **C1:** Reuse `pe_large_teacher_anchor.anchor` unchanged. Put it only in a copied step that logs CE, rank and anchor separately and keeps the bank refresh on the student's raw output.\n- **C2:** Take the shared prefix from a forward hook on the output of `encoder.layers[9]`, so the student's graph stays byte-identical. Build the teacher as a GPU `deepcopy` of layers 10\u201323, post-LN, pool and the compact head, taken inside `initialize` right after the source load. Set `requires_grad_(False)` and `.eval()`, and require fingerprint equality with the saved source keys. That is equivalent to a strict load, uses no RNG and puts nothing on the host.\n- **C3:** Bind the teacher fingerprint and the hook/code hash into the resume identity. Leave the payload keys unchanged so the teacher stays out of the checkpoint and a restart rebuilds it from the source.\n- **C4:** Add per-step asserts that teacher gradients are None, `_version` is unchanged, and no teacher parameter is in the optimizer. At step 1, assert the anchor is exactly zero with zero student anchor gradient, in mechanics and in every candidate arm.\n- **C5:** Do the whole-source calibration by strict-loading the source into the model `strict_reload` already builds, not a third host model. Show by arithmetic that it fits in 120s before launch.\n- **C6:** The fresh controls should reproduce the archived late100 control checkpoints bitwise (for seed 179032, `b40c8e4d\u2026`). A mismatch blocks paired scoring until it is explained.\n\n## Smallest falsifiers (no GPU)\n- **F0 (no cost; decides this REJECT):** add to the gate the required gain over the source (+0.208/+0.265pp) and one mechanism that creates it rather than preserves quality. If none is named, the recipe stays closed.\n- **F1 (source):** diff the new step against `step` and confirm the only difference is `+anchor` plus the teacher asserts.\n- **F2 (CPU):** on the two fixed fit images:\n  - The teacher's suffix/head output from the hook-captured layer-9 tensor must equal the whole-source `pooler_output` bitwise, and the int8 packed codes must match.\n  - Perturbing one student suffix weight must give an anchor above zero, finite nonzero student gradients, and no teacher gradients.\n  - All fingerprints and the RNG state must be restored exactly afterwards.\n- **F3 (arithmetic before mechanics):** 107.82s + 26 \u00d7 (measured extra seconds per step) + measured CPU teacher-setup time must stay under 120s, and the host RSS headroom must hold. If either fails, do not launch.",
